---
title: "Assignment 5: Visualization Audit"
format: html
execute:
  message: false
---

The flawed script selected only the first and last NHANES cycles, omitted its stated age restriction, and used a narrow y-axis. It also described mean BMI as obesity and made a causal claim. This revision includes every available cycle, restricts the data to adults aged 20–80, counts each income-by-cycle group, and places zero on the y-axis.

The figure remains a descriptive classroom summary. Its means are unweighted, so the lines connect observed cycle summaries rather than estimating annual population trends or the effect of income on BMI.



```{r}
# AI prompt: "Load the classroom CSV with repository-relative paths and check the variables needed for the BMI audit."

# Verified: Column names were checked against the supplied CSV; this R code ran locally.


library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

candidate_paths <- c(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  "../../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv"
)

existing_paths <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)]
if (length(existing_paths) == 0) {
  stop("Could not find examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv")
}

data_path <- existing_paths[[1]]
repo_prefix <- if (data_path == candidate_paths[[1]]) "." else "../../.."
nhanes <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

required_columns <- c("Cycle", "IncomeGroup", "BMI", "Age")
stopifnot(all(required_columns %in% names(nhanes)))

cycle_levels <- sort(unique(nhanes$Cycle[!is.na(nhanes$Cycle)]))
```





```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-alt: "Line and point chart of unweighted mean BMI across available NHANES cycles for three income groups among adults aged 20 to 80. The y-axis starts at zero."

# AI prompt: "Revise the flawed plot using all available NHANES cycles and adults aged 20–80. Exclude missing values, calculate each income-group-by-cycle cell count and unweighted mean BMI, retain cells with n >= 30, use a y-axis that includes zero, write descriptive labels and a caption covering the source, exclusions, and limitations, and export corrected-plot.png."

# Verified: The R code produced 33 cells, all with n >= 1,089. The zero-based plot and exported PNG were inspected.



bmi_by_income_cycle <- nhanes |>
  filter(
    !is.na(Cycle),
    !is.na(IncomeGroup),
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(Age),
    Age >= 20,
    Age <= 80
  ) |>
  group_by(Cycle, IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = mean(BMI, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(n >= 30) |>
  mutate(Cycle = factor(Cycle, levels = cycle_levels))

stopifnot(nrow(bmi_by_income_cycle) > 0)

caption_text <- paste(
  "This figure shows mean BMI (kg/m²) by income group across the available NHANES cycles using the prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom dataset.",
  "The summary is descriptive and unweighted.",
  "Records with missing BMI, income group, or cycle were excluded, as were records outside ages 20–80; only cycle–income cells with at least 30 records are shown.",
  "The plot supports comparison of patterns, not causal claims or population-level estimates."
)

corrected_plot <- ggplot(
  bmi_by_income_cycle,
  aes(x = Cycle, y = mean_bmi, color = IncomeGroup, group = IncomeGroup)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean BMI by income group across available NHANES cycles",
    subtitle = "Adults aged 20–80 in the prepared classroom dataset; unweighted",
    x = "NHANES cycle",
    y = "Mean BMI (kg/m²)",
    color = "Income group",
    caption = paste(strwrap(caption_text, width = 100), collapse = "\n")
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 8))
  )

plot_path <- file.path(
  repo_prefix,
  "assignments",
  "assignment05-visualization",
  "submission",
  "corrected-plot.png"
)

ggsave(
  filename = plot_path,
  plot = corrected_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)

corrected_plot
```
